# Implications for Current Skill Authors

What changes for someone already writing skills as local markdown files.

## The Short Answer: Nothing Changes Yet

SEP-2640 is In Review [13]. No MCP client supports skill:// natively [14].
If you are writing skills as local SKILL.md files for Claude Code today,
nothing about your workflow needs to change right now.

## What SEP-2640 Means for Your Skills

### Your format is already compatible

SEP-2640 builds on the Agent Skills specification [3][12], which defines
the same SKILL.md format you're already using. If your skills have `name`
and `description` in frontmatter and follow the directory structure
(SKILL.md + optional scripts/references/assets), they are Agent Skills
spec-compliant [12].

**Caveat:** Claude Code-specific frontmatter fields (`hooks`, `agent`,
`model`, `context`, `user-invocable`, `disable-model-invocation`) are
NOT part of the Agent Skills spec [11][12]. Skills using these fields
work in Claude Code but are not portable to other platforms and would
not be meaningful over MCP [11].

### What MCP transport would add

If/when clients adopt SEP-2640, your skills could be:

1. **Served from MCP servers** instead of local files [3]
2. **Discovered automatically** when connecting to a server [3]
3. **Updated dynamically** without reinstalling [4]
4. **Available ephemerally** without permanent disk footprint [4]
5. **Composed across servers** spanning tools from multiple MCP
   servers [4][6]

### What MCP transport would NOT change

- **Format stays the same** — SKILL.md + frontmatter + supporting files [3]
- **Local skills continue to work** — the spec says hosts SHOULD treat
  filesystem and MCP skills identically [3]
- **No new runtime behavior** — skills remain instructional data,
  not executable code [3][9]

## When to Care About This

**Care now if:** you build skills that are tightly coupled to an MCP
server's tools and want to distribute them as a package [4][6].

**Care later if:** you build standalone skills for personal use —
local files serve this use case fine and SEP-2640 explicitly lists
"standalone skills with no server dependency" as a case where "simpler
alternatives suffice" [4].

**Care when it ships:** once MCP clients support skill:// natively,
converting a local skill to an MCP-served skill is mechanical — add
it to an MCP server that exposes skill:// resources [3]. The
skillsovermcp.com service already demonstrates this for GitHub-hosted
skills [14].

## Migration Path (When Applicable)

### Making a local skill MCP-servable

1. Ensure frontmatter uses only Agent Skills spec fields (name,
   description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools) [12]
2. Move Claude Code-specific fields (hooks, agent, model) to the
   host configuration rather than the skill itself
3. Host the skill directory in an MCP server that exposes skill://
   resources (or use skillsovermcp.com for GitHub repos) [14]
4. The skill content stays identical — only the delivery changes

### What you lose in the MCP transport

The security model is stricter for MCP-served skills [3]:
- **No implicit execution** — hooks, scripts, shell commands in MCP
  skills require explicit user approval [3]
- **Untrusted input** — MCP skills are treated as untrusted, subject
  to prompt injection defenses [3]
- **No elevated authority** — skills cannot supersede user policy [3]

This means skills that rely on hooks executing automatically (like
PreToolUse validators or PostToolUse formatters) cannot be
transparently served over MCP without the host explicitly opting in
to execute them.

## Gaps and Limitations

- No timeline for when MCP clients will support skill:// [13]
- Non-standard frontmatter fields create a portability gap [11]
- Model adherence to skill instructions is "time-decaying" regardless
  of transport [7] — MCP delivery doesn't solve this
- Plugin/bundle packaging (skills + servers + hooks as one artifact)
  is out of scope for SEP-2640 [13]
